m8-t1.introduction: Turn course artefacts into a compact evidence story. Lead with the work that fits the role and make the proof easy to inspect.

sections.title: PARE makes the case study inspectable
sections.explanation: A case study joins the business problem to your decisions, a measured result and evidence.

items.label: Problem
items.detail: State the starting situation and constraint honestly.

items.label: Action
items.detail: Describe your decisions and personal contribution.

items.label: Result
items.detail: Report a defined outcome against a baseline.

items.label: Evidence
items.detail: Show a redacted screenshot, table or working artefact.

sections.takeaway: Add what you would change next. Never present a practice dataset as a live client result.

sections.title: The first case should match the job
sections.explanation: The same projects can support different applications when the lead story changes.

items.label: Marketing Executive
items.detail: Lead with the integrated campaign and content execution.

items.label: SEO Executive
items.detail: Lead with the evidence-based audit and keyword-to-page work.

items.label: Marketing Analyst
items.detail: Lead with the dashboard, insight log and experiment design.

sections.takeaway: Use the job description to choose the order; do not inflate your contribution to make it fit.

sections.section: 2. The three target roles and their evidence

sections.title: Make a short path from identity to proof
sections.explanation: A simple page is enough if it is readable, accessible and easy to open.

items.label: Identity
items.detail: Name the target role and a concise line of evidence.

items.label: Selected cases
items.detail: Curate a few complete stories rather than raw exports.

items.label: Proof / credentials
items.detail: Provide inspectable artefacts and accurately stated awards.

items.label: Contact
items.detail: Offer an appropriate professional contact route and résumé.

sections.takeaway: Check permissions and remove customer-identifying or confidential material before sharing.
sections.caption: Concept illustration, not a platform screenshot. Follow the labels and the relationships shown.

sections.title: Experience can be small and still be real
sections.explanation: A local project becomes credible through a real constraint, a stakeholder and documented decisions.

items.label: Real small project
items.detail: Show the actual scope, budget and stakeholder involvement.

items.label: Course / practice project
items.detail: Label the setting and the simulated parts clearly.

items.label: What you learned
items.detail: Explain the trade-off, failure and next improvement.

sections.takeaway: Honest self-generated work is stronger than invented employment or fabricated performance.
sections.caption: Concept illustration, not a platform screenshot. Follow the labels and the relationships shown.

sections.title: Use the scan test as a design rehearsal
sections.explanation: The reading’s time boxes help test whether the page exposes the right information quickly. They are not a universal recruiter behaviour measurement.

items.label: First glance
items.detail: Can a stranger identify the role you want?

items.label: First case
items.detail: Can they see a meaningful number with context?

items.label: Quick inspection
items.detail: Can they open at least two pieces of evidence?

sections.takeaway: If the proof is buried, improve the reading order before adding another project.

checkpoint.question: Can a practice campaign appear in a portfolio?
checkpoint.answer: Yes, when its practice status, simulated data and your contribution are explicit. It must not be presented as a live client outcome.

m8-t2.introduction: Make the résumé, profile and certificates point to the same credible story. Track applications as a process you can improve.

sections.title: Build a résumé for a useful scan
sections.explanation: A focused résumé makes the target role, relevant skills and evidence visible without a long introduction.

items.label: Target role
items.detail: Use a role-specific heading and concise identity.

items.label: Relevant evidence
items.detail: Lead with projects and decisions that match the job.

items.label: Skills / credentials
items.detail: List only what you can explain or demonstrate.

items.label: Access
items.detail: Make contact and portfolio links work in the exported file.

sections.takeaway: Prefer clean structure and readable text over decorative layouts that obscure information.
sections.caption: Concept illustration, not a platform screenshot. Follow the labels and the relationships shown.
sections.section: 1. The résumé: structure for the scan

sections.title: A strong bullet shows the mechanism
sections.explanation: Connect the action to what you changed and the result you can support.

items.label: Verb
items.detail: Audited, built, analysed or improved.

items.label: Mechanism
items.detail: Explain the method or operational change.

items.label: Result / scope
items.detail: Use a verified outcome, or an honest deliverable if results are unavailable.

items.label: Evidence
items.detail: Keep the artefact ready for an interview follow-up.

sections.takeaway: Do not invent a percentage just because quantified bullets look impressive.
sections.caption: Concept illustration, not a platform screenshot. Follow the labels and the relationships shown.
sections.section: 2. The bullet pattern: verb + mechanism + result

sections.title: A profile should be findable and credible
sections.explanation: Use relevant professional language while making the proof easy to inspect.

items.label: Headline
items.detail: Name the role focus and practical skills honestly.

items.label: About
items.detail: Explain the kind of problem you can help solve.

items.label: Featured work
items.detail: Link a small set of appropriate evidence cases.

items.label: Consistency
items.detail: Keep dates, claims and contact routes aligned with the résumé.

sections.takeaway: Keyword stuffing cannot replace a clear work story and a useful portfolio.
sections.caption: Concept illustration, not a platform screenshot. Follow the labels and the relationships shown.

sections.title: A credential has a precise status
sections.explanation: Keep completed, in-progress and planned learning distinct.

items.label: Earned
items.detail: Use the actual award name, issuer and verification link where available.

items.label: In progress
items.detail: State that it is unfinished without implying certification.

items.label: Planned
items.detail: Treat it as a learning goal, not an earned qualification.

sections.takeaway: A certificate supports evidence of skill; it is not a guarantee of competence or employment.

sections.section: 4. Certifications: which, why, and honest presentation

sections.title: Run applications as a feedback system
sections.explanation: A small application log helps you follow up and learn where the process is breaking down.

items.label: Select
items.detail: Choose roles that fit the evidence you can show.

items.label: Tailor
items.detail: Reorder the résumé and portfolio honestly.

items.label: Track
items.detail: Record date, stage, contact and next action.

items.label: Review
items.detail: Use response and interview feedback to improve.

sections.takeaway: Quality and relevance matter more than sending the same document everywhere.
sections.caption: Concept illustration, not a platform screenshot. Follow the labels and the relationships shown.

checkpoint.question: What should a result bullet say if there is no reliable performance data?
checkpoint.answer: Describe the real deliverable, method and scope without inventing impact. For example, say you audited two pages and produced an evidence-backed roadmap, then show it.

m8-t3.introduction: Practise explaining decisions, not reciting tool names. Use a structure for behavioural stories, a separate frame for new cases and evidence for every result.

sections.title: STAR-R turns experience into a clear answer
sections.explanation: The reflection step shows what changed in your judgement after the result.

items.label: Situation / task
items.detail: State the context, goal and real constraints.

items.label: Action
items.detail: Explain your decisions and why you chose them.

items.label: Result
items.detail: Use a defined number with a baseline and evidence.

items.label: Reflection
items.detail: Say what you would repeat or do differently.

sections.takeaway: Be explicit about your own contribution when the project was a team effort.
sections.caption: Concept illustration, not a platform screenshot. Follow the labels and the relationships shown.

sections.title: G-S-M-A-P is a thinking order
sections.explanation: Use the case frame to expose assumptions before prescribing tactics.

items.label: Goal & metrics
items.detail: Restate the objective and cost or quality guardrails.

items.label: Situation & audience
items.detail: Ask for missing context and customer evidence.

items.label: Strategy & mix
items.detail: Choose channel roles with a reason.

items.label: Actions & timeline
items.detail: Sequence foundations, launch and learning.

items.label: Prediction & measurement
items.detail: Show the arithmetic, assumptions and review rule.

sections.takeaway: Acknowledge uncertainty. A neat framework does not make invented estimates factual.
sections.caption: Concept illustration, not a platform screenshot. Follow the labels and the relationships shown.

sections.title: A failure story can demonstrate judgement
sections.explanation: Own the miss without hiding behind a platform or a teammate.

items.label: Miss
items.detail: Name what failed against the target.

items.label: Diagnosis
items.detail: Explain the evidence and what remains uncertain.

items.label: Change
items.detail: Describe the action and its observed outcome.

items.label: Transfer
items.detail: State the rule you now apply to similar work.

sections.takeaway: Do not turn a small sample or a before/after comparison into an unsupported causal claim.
sections.caption: Concept illustration, not a platform screenshot. Follow the labels and the relationships shown.

sections.title: Build an evidence shelf for common questions
sections.explanation: Prepare reusable stories, then adapt them to the actual question rather than memorising a monologue.

items.label: Execution story
items.detail: A campaign or content decision with constraints and proof.

items.label: Diagnosis story
items.detail: An SEO or CPA problem investigated in a sensible order.

items.label: People story
items.detail: A feedback or community incident handled responsibly.

items.label: Learning story
items.detail: A failure that changed your next decision.

sections.takeaway: Keep an honest tool demonstration ready and ask useful questions about the role and team.

sections.section: 4. The ten questions you will face

sections.title: Rehearse the answer, inspect the evidence
sections.explanation: Speaking aloud exposes gaps that silent preparation misses.

items.label: Speak
items.detail: Answer a shuffled question aloud within the time limit.

items.label: Record
items.detail: Review clarity, pace and unsupported claims.

items.label: Peer challenge
items.detail: Ask a partner to question the number or decision.

items.label: Revise
items.detail: Improve the reasoning and evidence, then repeat.

sections.takeaway: Keep the portfolio open and offer the evidence when you cite a result.
sections.caption: Concept illustration, not a platform screenshot. Follow the labels and the relationships shown.

checkpoint.question: What is a stronger response to “why did the campaign fail” than “the algorithm changed”?
checkpoint.answer: State the miss, show the diagnosis and its limits, explain the action you took, and describe the lesson you now apply. Separate evidence from a convenient explanation.

m8-cap.introduction: Connect the whole course into one honest campaign story. Plan the live run early enough to meet the minimum duration, then show evidence, consent and learning at Demo Day.

sections.title: The capstone joins strategy, execution and learning
sections.explanation: A campaign is complete only when its channels, relationship and measurement reinforce one another.

items.label: Plan
items.detail: Choose the client, audience, goal, baseline and constraints.

items.label: Launch
items.detail: Use at least three channels including an owned route.

items.label: Run / improve
items.detail: Observe, experiment and apply the pre-set decision rules.

items.label: Explain
items.detail: Present results, limits, failure and the next recommendation.

sections.takeaway: Protect at least two full weeks of campaign operation. Preparation and pitch work do not replace the required run.
sections.caption: Concept illustration, not a platform screenshot. Follow the labels and the relationships shown.

sections.title: Make the campaign pack a traceable story
sections.explanation: An assessor should be able to follow the chain from the first goal to the final recommendation.

items.label: Strategy + assets
items.detail: One-pager, channel assets and the calendar.

items.label: Consent + measurement
items.detail: Permission copy, working exit, event plan and dashboard.

items.label: Journal + experiment
items.detail: At least three entries, an experiment and a kill / scale decision.

items.label: Results + failure
items.detail: Report against baselines and analyse the weakest element.

items.label: Disclosure + pitch
items.detail: Specific AI-use statement and a rehearsed five-minute presentation.

sections.takeaway: Use the original ordered submission list. Keep customer details and confidential business information out of public evidence.
sections.caption: Concept illustration, not a platform screenshot. Follow the labels and the relationships shown.

sections.title: Show the course connections explicitly
sections.explanation: The capstone assesses integration, so make the dependency between modules visible.

items.label: Foundations + SEO + content
items.detail: Use the brief, useful search or listing work and a content strategy.

items.label: Paid or social execution
items.detail: Run appropriate real channel operations with constraints disclosed.

items.label: Analytics
items.detail: Keep the dashboard, experiment and insight ritual active.

items.label: Lifecycle + consent
items.detail: Use a permitted relationship or CRM route with a working exit.

sections.takeaway: Numbers without consent and launches without measurement both miss the integration requirement.
sections.caption: Concept illustration, not a platform screenshot. Follow the labels and the relationships shown.

sections.title: Schedule backwards from the required run
sections.explanation: Confirm dates with the facilitator so setup, a minimum two-week run and the final presentation can all fit.

items.label: Before launch
items.detail: Lock access, goal, baseline, consent, assets and tested tracking.

items.label: Run for at least 14 days
items.detail: Operate channels, record the required journal entries and test responsibly.

items.label: Close the evidence
items.detail: Pull comparable results and record failures and decisions.

items.label: Rehearse / present
items.detail: Time the pitch, check links and prepare for questions.

sections.takeaway: If the calendar cannot accommodate the minimum run, resolve the schedule before launch rather than claiming a shorter period meets it.
sections.caption: Concept illustration, not a platform screenshot. Follow the labels and the relationships shown.

sections.title: A professional pitch makes the evidence easy to challenge
sections.explanation: The strongest presentation can explain both the useful result and the limitation behind it.

items.label: Strategy + execution
items.detail: Show the reason for the channel mix and what actually ran.

items.label: Measurement + integrity
items.detail: Show baselines, defined outcomes and labelled practice data.

items.label: Lifecycle + learning
items.detail: Show consent, iteration and what a failure changed.

items.label: Communication
items.detail: Use the five-minute format and answer with evidence.

sections.takeaway: The original capstone rubric, pass conditions and live-presentation requirement remain unchanged.
sections.caption: Concept illustration, not a platform screenshot. Follow the labels and the relationships shown.

checkpoint.question: Does a polished pitch compensate for a campaign that ran for less than two weeks?
checkpoint.answer: No. Check the original minimum run and coverage rules. Plan earlier or agree a revised schedule with the facilitator; never relabel a shorter run or invent missing journal evidence.
